statusText: CME equity-index futures have been shut since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and do not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, so there is no observable NQ price path this hour and none anywhere in the 24-hour horizon, which ends at 05:00 UTC on 16 August - still about 17 hours before the reopen. Tail is 10% (low), holding the action at EA_ON and the status green: pathological one-way structure cannot form while no venue is quoting, and the low non-zero level prices weekend headline discontinuity rather than any observed extension. The one-point rise from 9% is driven by genuinely new escalation since the last run rather than by price behaviour - Lebanese state media report an Israeli strike on the outskirts of Ansar in southern Lebanon early Saturday that killed seven and wounded three, the worst toll since the 26 June framework agreement, with the Times of Israel reporting heavy accompanying strikes on the Ali Taher ridge in the Nabatieh area. The last confirmed structure, re-verified this hour, is unchanged: NQ futures settled at 30,148.25, down 40.25 points or 0.13%, mid-range inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band, while the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14 (-0.13%) in a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range and about 2.3% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20, with VIX at 14.25 (-2.60%) and H.15 showing 2Y 4.15%, 10Y 4.63% and 30Y 5.21%. Stress firms from 45% to 48% (elevated) because the escalation set widened rather than resolved: the strait is still shut, the U.S. naval blockade is still in force with 59 vessels redirected since 13 July, the UAE has blamed Iran for drone attacks on two ADNOC tankers in the strait on Thursday evening, Hegseth has said the blockade can hold indefinitely and Bessent has previewed unprecedented curbs ahead of a reported 17 August deadline, WTI sits at $82.40 and Brent at $88.52 after a weekly gain of about 5%, and Friday's U.S. consumer data was sharply soft with Retail Sales -0.6% against +0.1% expected and Michigan sentiment 51.0 against 54.5. Confidence is 59% (medium-low): everything except the price path is fresh and primary-sourced, but the price path is the input that matters most and it does not exist this hour. The operative checkpoint remains the Sunday CME reopen, which the danger window brackets.
recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (10%) alone. No venue is quoting NQ anywhere in the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it, so there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The operative checkpoint is the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, where a full weekend of accumulated headlines would express as an opening gap rather than as intraday structure - the danger window brackets that reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery. Gap risk is genuinely two-way and the weekend has added to both sides of it: escalation from the Ansar strike, the ADNOC tanker attacks, an indefinite blockade posture and a reported 17 August sanctions deadline pull one way, while the unsigned but reportedly close Iran-Oman routing arrangement and Tehran's stated willingness to reopen on terms pull the other. Crude can move before equities are able to price it, and Friday's weak consumer prints leave a second, unrelated growth-scare channel open into the 19 August FOMC minutes. This is a general market-risk assessment for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and no trade is being placed or recommended.
headline: New Middle East escalation lands into a shut market: an Israeli strike killed seven at Ansar in southern Lebanon early Saturday and the UAE has blamed Iran for drone attacks on two ADNOC tankers in Hormuz, but with CME closed until Sunday there is no price path to score - Tail stays low at 10% on EA_ON while Stress firms to 48%.
body:
PRICE PATH (observed, stale by necessity). No venue has quoted NQ since the CME weekly close at 21:00 UTC on Friday 14 August, and none will until the Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August. The last live structure, re-verified this hour from primary sources, remains benign: September E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures settled at 30,148.25, -40.25 points or -0.13%, against a previous close of 30,188.50, finishing mid-range inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band - roughly 254 points wide, or 0.84% - with no close near either extreme. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14, -38.36 points or -0.13%, inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range, about 2.3% below the 52-week high of 30,762.20 and well above the 22,841.42 low. A two-way intraday range with a mid-range settle is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks and repeated extension that the Tail definition requires. Directional efficiency, pullback depth, failed-retracement counts and proximity to session extremes are all unobservable this hour; that is a structural absence of evidence, not evidence of calm, and it is the single reason Confidence stays medium-low.

CROSS-ASSET (observed, Friday close). VIX closed at 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60%, in a 14.18-14.72 day range and near the bottom of its 13.38-35.30 52-week band - the options market priced no stress into the weekend. The latest H.15 constant-maturity yields, for 13 August, are 2Y 4.15%, 10Y 4.63% and 30Y 5.21%: a positively sloped curve with no acute front-end repricing. Crude is the one asset carrying the geopolitical premium, and it is carrying it clearly - WTI $82.40, +$1.15 or +1.42% on the day and roughly +5% on the week, +3.52% on the month; Brent $88.52, +$1.45 or +1.67% on the day, also about +5% on the week and +34.43% year-over-year. This is a textbook conflicting-signal set: equity volatility asleep, rates orderly, energy repricing a supply shock. Per the risk definitions, conflicting signals belong in Stress, not Tail, and that is exactly where they are scored.

GEOPOLITICS (new escalation this run). Two developments postdate the previous assessment. First, Lebanon's state news agency reports an Israeli airstrike on the outskirts of Ansar, north of Tyre, early Saturday that destroyed a home and killed seven with three wounded - the deadliest strike since the 26 June framework agreement under which Israeli forces would withdraw from southern Lebanon in exchange for Hezbollah disarmament; the Times of Israel additionally reports some of the heaviest strikes yet on the Ali Taher ridge in the Nabatieh area, above a major Hezbollah underground facility. Second, the UAE has blamed Iran for drone attacks on two ADNOC-linked tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday evening, with UKMTO confirming minor damage and no casualties. Alongside those, the standing impasse is intact and hardening: the Persian Gulf Strait Authority says the strait 'remains blocked and will not be reopened until Iran's conditions are accepted', chiefly sanctions relief and the release of frozen assets; U.S. Central Command has redirected 59 commercial vessels since reimposing the blockade on 13 July; War Secretary Hegseth says the blockade can hold indefinitely; Treasury Secretary Bessent has promised economic isolation 'like the world has never seen' with further announcements next week ahead of a reported 17 August deadline; Trump told a New York rally he would declare the strait U.S. territory, and Iran's deputy foreign minister replied early Saturday that it 'cannot be seized by tweet'; and the Iran-Oman routing arrangement remains unsigned. The IEA continues to warn of the widest global supply deficit in five years for 2026 as stockpiles draw down. This is a live, unresolved escalation with a demonstrated transmission channel into crude and, through crude, into the growth and inflation backdrop - it is not the mere existence of conflict.

MACRO (observed). Friday's U.S. consumer prints both missed sharply: Retail Sales -0.6% month-over-month against +0.1% consensus and +0.2% prior, and preliminary August Michigan sentiment 51.0 against 54.5 consensus and 55.2 prior. Equities absorbed those misses on Friday with two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency - the reason Tail sat at 7-9% through the cash session while Stress built to the low 40s. The soft-consumer channel is a second, independent thread into the 19 August FOMC minutes, unrelated to the Middle East. No U.S. macro release falls inside this 24-hour horizon; the calendar restarts with the NY Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC on Monday 17 August.

SCORING (inference). Tail 10% - low band, EA_ON, green. A shut venue cannot produce a pathological price path, and none of the amplifier conditions the contract requires for 25%+ is observable, let alone confirmed. The one-point increase over the last six hours is an honest accounting of widened weekend headline discontinuity risk, not a claim about structure. Stress 48% - elevated, up three points, because the escalation set widened while nothing resolved, and because a shut market defers rather than removes the repricing. Confidence 59% - medium-low. Every obtainable input was obtained and verified against primary sources this hour; the gap is structural, and a weekend futures halt with no live price path is precisely the case the contract reserves the medium-low band for. Dominant mode is mixed: a halted tape overlaid on genuinely conflicting cross-asset signals and two-way geopolitical threads.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 2-9% throughout. It held 9% through Friday's Asian and European sessions, eased to 7-9% across the U.S. cash session as the sharp Retail Sales and Michigan sentiment misses produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency, and printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close. Stress described a clear event arc: 25-28% in the quiet Friday pre-dawn and morning hours, building to 40-44% through the U.S. cash session as the data landed, then 34% at the close. The two runs immediately after the close scored the halt itself at Tail 2% and Stress 12%; from 00:00 UTC onward that reading was corrected back to Tail 9% and Stress 45% on the judgement that a shut venue does not neutralise a live Hormuz closure, and 45% then held for six consecutive hours through 05:00 UTC. Those past opinions are preserved exactly as published and have not been rewritten. Confidence spent the Friday session in the 30s-50s and firmed to 56-59% after midnight as primary-source verification improved. One slot, 20:00 UTC on 14 August, has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it runs from 06:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 05:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly 17 hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is therefore projected flat at 10% for the first fourteen slots and ticking to 11% from 20:00 UTC on 15 August as the reopen edges into view; that increment reflects accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays deep in the low band, so the action is EA_ON and the status green throughout. Stress is projected to ease at most a point to 47% through the thin Saturday European and U.S. afternoon hours, when weekend headline flow is historically lightest, then firm back to 48-49% into the late slots as unresolved threads converge on Sunday's price discovery: the Hormuz impasse and Tehran's insistence on sanctions relief first, the indefinite-blockade posture and the reported 17 August deadline for unprecedented new curbs, the fresh Lebanon escalation and its bearing on the June framework, the unsigned Iran-Oman routing arrangement, and a soft U.S. consumer picture heading into the 19 August FOMC minutes. Confidence stays in the medium-low band at 58-59% for as long as no venue quotes. The real checkpoint sits just beyond this horizon: the reopen at roughly 22:00 UTC on 16 August, which the danger window brackets together with its first 90 minutes of trade. Gap risk there is two-way, and the first live tape - not this forecast - is what will decide whether Tail leaves the low band.

Confidence stays medium-low at 59% - every non-price input is fresh and primary-sourced, but the price path, the input that matters most, does not exist.

U.S. Saturday afternoon. Roughly 34 hours remain to the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday. Tail holds at 10% and the status stays green; the accumulating gap risk is real but is still more than a day away and is genuinely two-way, with a reported 17 August U.S. sanctions deadline and the unsigned Iran-Oman routing arrangement pulling in opposite directions.
